prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a spacious indoor concourse with a receding floor plane, ceiling, central structural column (~6-7 m away), and a kiosk on the left (~5-6 m away), surrounding a group of five women standing ~1-3.5 m in front of the camera wearer and ~0.5-1.5 m apart from each other. In frame 1, the woman in the grey top (front-right) and the woman in the yellow hoodie (front-left) are brightest and closest (~1-1.5 m, within or near the camera wearer's arm's reach, with their lower bodies cropped at the bottom frame edge), while the women in the maroon jacket (far left, ~2-2.5 m), striped pink top (behind yellow, ~3 m), and patterned beige jacket (center, ~2.5-3 m) stand further back and within arm's reach of their immediate neighbors. Across the 5 frames, the yellow-hoodie woman moves from front-left (frames 1-2) toward the center-right and gets progressively brighter/nearer until she enters extreme close-up (~0.5-0.8 m, well within arm's reach) at the bottom-right in frame 5, increasingly occluding the striped-shirt woman in frames 2-4 and the lower torso of the grey-shirt woman in frame 5, while background pedestrians walk leftward from behind the central group (~4-5 m) toward the left kiosk (~5-6 m). The depth map clearly separates foreground depth layers (such as the yellow-hoodie woman stepping in front of the maroon-jacket and striped-shirt women) and floor-to-column geometry that flatten out in the wide-angle RGB, though it lacks facial and gaze detail—where RGB shows the yellow-hoodie woman looking toward the camera wearer in frames 1-4 before turning away in frame 5 while the others mostly face inward toward the group—and blurs boundary depths around flying hair and distant background pedestrians.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and background people along with a few wall-mounted objects against a black background, showing five main foreground `person` masks clustered ~0.5-3.5 m in front of the camera wearer (spaced ~0.5-1.5 m apart) and smaller background `person` masks ~4-7 m behind them near the ATM/kiosk on the left. Across frames 1 to 5, as the yellow-hoodie woman's mask shifts from bottom-left (~1.5 m) to bottom-right (~0.5-0.8 m, within the camera wearer's arm's reach), her mask overlaps and occludes the striped-shirt woman behind her (whose mask disappears completely by frame 5) and partially occludes the grey-shirt woman on the right in frame 5, while two pedestrians (~4-6 m away, within arm's reach of each other) emerge from behind the center-left group in frame 2 and walk leftward with a `handbag` (actually a white pack/bag carried at hip level) detected in frames 4-5. This map highlights distant, partially occluded background pedestrians near the green ATM and a small screen (`tv`) high on the upper-left/upper-right edge (~6-8 m away, above head level) that are easy to overlook in the busy RGB strip. However, the map is unreliable in several places: it misclassifies the painted mural figure on the back wall (~8-10 m away, upper right of the central pillar) as a `person` in frames 3-5, fragments or drops masks for heavily occluded background people, and provides only 2D silhouettes that cannot show 3D distances or whether people face the camera wearer.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D yellow body keypoints on a black background, completely omitting the room layout, background pedestrians, and four of the five foreground women who stand ~1-3.5 m from the camera wearer. In frame 1, it detects only the upper body and raised arms of the woman in the patterned beige jacket (standing center, ~2.5-3 m away, facing roughly toward the camera wearer and foreground group with her hands raised to her head), whereas in frames 2 through 5 it switches to tracking only the head/face and a single torso-to-hip line of the woman in the grey top on the right (~1.2-1.8 m away, facing left in profile toward the group rather than toward the camera wearer, within arm's reach of the yellow-hoodie woman by frame 5). While these sparse keypoints trace the grey-shirt woman's subtle torso shifts and leftward head orientation on the right side of the frame across frames 2-5 without visual clutter, almost all spatial context must be inferred from the RGB image. The map is highly unreliable overall: it misses all magenta hand skeletons despite visible hands within arm's reach of the subjects' own heads and torsos, fails to detect the approaching yellow-hoodie woman (~0.5-1.5 m away, cropped at the lower boundary) and the left-side women entirely, and produces distorted, incomplete stick segments in every frame.
